scope: Five supplied full originals with targeted page and visual checks. Embedded repeats are not independent corroboration. No new evidence-request closures.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: Signed Missaukee–Wexford agreement identifies the landfill as a primary disposal site
events.finding: Missaukee County and the Wexford County Board of Public Works executed a reciprocal solid-waste disposal agreement. Section 2.3 requires an authorized commercial-hauler list; tipping fees are generally payable on delivery and set by separate DPW resolution. The initial five-year term requires mutual agreement for renewal.
events.significance: This is Missaukee solid waste → Wexford landfill, not Wexford leachate → Cadillac WWTP. It identifies hauler-list and fee-record leads but supplies no actual load tickets, numerical rate schedule or later executed renewals.

sources.name: Missaukee Solid Waste Plan Compilation — Signed 1995 Wexford DPW Disposal Agreement.pdf
sources.result: PDF pp136–143 contain the signed September 19, 1995 agreement; p140 §2.3 covers hauler lists and p141 §§4.1–4.2 covers fees and payment.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: Wexford DPW certifies capacity for Missaukee at then-current volumes
events.finding: In a signed October 13, 1998 letter, Wexford DPW Director Gary R. Fuller states that the landfill has sufficient capacity for Missaukee County’s use for the next ten years at then-current solid-waste volumes.
events.significance: A dated historical capacity assurance, not a transaction ledger, a modern capacity estimate or proof of individual deliveries.

sources.name: Missaukee Solid Waste Plan Compilation — Signed 1995 Wexford DPW Disposal Agreement.pdf
sources.result: PDF p64 (printed III-30) is the signed capacity certification.

events.timeBasis: Month and year printed on the map; day and time not stated
events.title: CTI map locates Wexford landfill boundaries and disposal cells
events.finding: The February 2007 CTI facility map, project 75010002.2, Drawing 1, depicts landfill boundaries and cells at 1 inch = 600 feet. The same map is repeated on PDF pages 28 and 83 of this full 347-page compilation.
events.significance: The map supplies spatial site history, not groundwater-flow direction, a PFAS pathway or proof of any shipment. The two copies are the same map, not separate corroboration. No exact day is printed.

sources.name: Wexford Solid Waste Management Plan Compilation — Including February 2007 CTI Facility Map.pdf
sources.result: PDF pp28 and 83 contain repeated CTI maps. Nearby profiles pp27 and 82 list waste types, not delivered-load records.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: Meeting minutes connect landfill pricing discussion with contamination issues
events.finding: December 12, 2007 committee minutes attribute to Wexford landfill representative Richard Leszcz a statement that contamination issues contributed to higher Wexford prices, alongside discussion of attracting more waste and supporting recycling.
events.significance: This preserves the participant’s statement. It is not an independent causation finding, contaminant identification, PFAS result or delivery record.

sources.name: Missaukee Solid Waste Plan Compilation — Signed 1995 Wexford DPW Disposal Agreement.pdf
sources.result: PDF p5 preserves the December 12, 2007 discussion and attribution.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: State approves Wexford plan amendment with modifications
events.finding: The April 19, 2011 state letter approves the internally named 2009 amendment with modifications. Import tables list 22 counties with primary agreements and negotiated quantities; the export table lists five destinations. The County approved the amendment 7–2 on September 15, 2010.
events.significance: Read the approval letter together with the amended pages. Plan consistency is not a construction permit. These are planning authorizations, not actual waste or leachate delivery totals; the enclosed sample ordinance is not an executed ordinance.

sources.name: Wexford Solid Waste Management Plan Amendment — State Approval April 19, 2011.pdf
sources.result: PDF pp1–4: controlling approval/modifications; pp14–16: import/export tables; p46: County vote.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: Wexford plan removes the negotiated-agreement prerequisite
events.finding: The May 1, 2012 approval keeps the same 22 import counties but changes agreement-required/negotiated-volume entries to primary/unrestricted entries. It removes the negotiated executed-agreement prerequisite and expands export destinations from five to 22.
events.significance: Receiving-county approved-plan authorization and licensed-facility conditions remain. This historical planning change does not establish actual deliveries, cancel existing contracts or waive shipping documentation.

sources.name: Wexford Solid Waste Management Plan Amendment — State Approval May 1, 2012.pdf
sources.result: PDF pp1–2: approval; p4: deletion of D6 agreement prerequisite; pp7–8: replacement import/export tables.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: American Waste requests Lake County authorization for Wexford disposal
events.finding: American Waste Co-President Edward Ascione signs a May 14, 2014 request to add Wexford County to Lake County’s authorized solid-waste export destinations without conditions.
events.significance: This is the operator’s request, not state approval or a completed shipment. Lake’s 2016 approval is shown separately. It does not establish transport to Cadillac WWTP.

sources.name: Lake County Solid Waste Plan Amendment — Wexford Disposal Authorization, 2016.pdf
sources.result: PDF pp95–96 contain the original signed American Waste request.

events.timeBasis: Dated source record; time of day not stated
events.title: DEQ approves Lake County’s Wexford disposal authorization
events.finding: On August 31, 2016, DEQ approves Lake County’s amendment adding Wexford as a primary solid-waste disposal authorization; DEQ received the amendment June 7, 2016. The Wexford quantity cells are blank, not 100%.
events.significance: This completes the request-to-approval sequence, not a delivery sequence. The included Golder map depicts leachate infrastructure, including a 20,000-gallon backup tank, but not actual flow or hauling to Cadillac.
